subject: zoology
question_text: Distinguish the terms phototaxis and photokinesis.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack zoology section (book p.61, VSAQ 159). Zoology holds only ONE source book — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no zoology board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Phototaxis
lines: Phototaxis is the influence of light on the
DIRECTIONAL movement of an organism, either
towards the light or away from it.
Ex: Euglena moves towards light — positive
Ex: the cockroach moves away from light —
steps.why: The two examples are chosen to sit on opposite sides of the same term, which shows the examiner that the movement has a direction and that the direction can go either way.
common_mistakes: Writing that phototaxis is movement towards light only. It may be towards OR away.
Leaving out the words positive and negative, which name the two directions.
steps.memory_tip: Taxis has a direction: towards is positive, away is negative.
steps.margin_note: One sentence, then the two examples with their signs. Keep each example to one line.

steps.label: Photokinesis

lines.text: Taxis sets the direction, kinesis the speed

lines: Photokinesis is the influence of the
INTENSITY of light on the non-directional
Ex: the larva of Pinnotheres maculatus, the
mussel crab, moves faster as the light gets
brighter, but keeps its own direction.
steps.why: The contrast is not light against no light but direction against speed, so the second half must say non-directional and must tie the change to the INTENSITY of the light.
common_mistakes: Writing that the organism moves towards brighter light. In photokinesis the direction does not change.
Leaving out the word intensity. Photokinesis answers how BRIGHT the light is, not where it is.
steps.memory_tip: Kinesis is like kinetic — it is about speed. Taxis is about which way.
steps.margin_note: One sentence with non-directional and intensity in it, then the named example.

insider_note: The distinction the examiner marks is direction against speed — a student who writes towards the light in both halves loses one mark.
